Description: Accessibility and UX: command-center buttons and tab controls maintain approximately 40px minimum target sizes in the rendered browser, not only in source class markers.
User Story: As a keyboard, mouse, or touch user, I can reliably activate command-center controls without tiny click targets.
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given the command center renders at desktop and mobile sizes, when visible buttons and tab controls are measured in Chromium, then each visible button target is at least approximately 40px tall and 40px wide where applicable. 2. Icon-only contextual question actions are not smaller than 40px. 3. Regression evidence is recorded after CSS changes are built and browser-tested.
Expected Behavior: Visible command-center buttons, tabs, and icon actions render with at least approximately 40px target size in the browser.
Entry Points: Topbar actions, setup buttons, tab controls, select triggers, preview question actions, answer check buttons, mobile action bar, mobile sheet actions.
Edge Cases: Responsive desktop/mobile duplicate controls, icon-only lock/refresh buttons, small variant topbar buttons, tab triggers, Tailwind utility ordering in production CSS.
User Roles / Permissions: Teacher / worksheet creator; no auth or permission gates in scope.
Error / Empty / Loading States: Small target rendering can appear after responsive layout or utility-order changes even when source class markers exist.
Initial Test Evidence: failed: Fresh Chromium QA measured visible controls below 40px, including topbar New version/Print, tab triggers, select triggers, question lock/refresh buttons, and Check buttons.
Reproduction Steps: 1. Build and start the static preview. 2. Run Chromium against http://127.0.0.1:4173 at 1440px desktop. 3. Measure visible button bounding boxes. 4. Observe several controls with 32px, 34px, or 36px height.
Expected Result: Visible command-center controls maintain approximately 40px minimum target size.
Actual Result: Before fix, multiple visible controls rendered below 40px despite source-level min-h class markers.
Root Cause: Production CSS utility ordering allowed fixed height utilities such as h-8/h-9 to win over source-level min-h markers for rendered buttons.
Screenshots / Evidence: Fresh Chromium QA failure log in current run; screenshots refreshed at output/playwright/real-browser-desktop.png after retest. passed: Fresh Chromium QA verified visible desktop buttons keep approximately 40px minimum target size; see output/playwright/feature-story-real-browser-results.json.
Fix Summary: Added scoped .command-center-shell button CSS target-size enforcement, removed the scale-down hidden state from preview question actions, and added regression source assertions.
UX Improvement: Controls now have more reliable pointer/touch target sizes across desktop and mobile layouts.
Regression Evidence: passed: Fresh Chromium QA verified visible desktop buttons keep approximately 40px minimum target size; see output/playwright/feature-story-real-browser-results.json.

Description: Accessibility and UX: desktop view shows only the desktop command layout, while mobile view shows only the mobile step workflow and action bar.
User Story: As a teacher, I see one coherent command-center layout for my viewport instead of duplicate mobile and desktop workflows at the same time.
Acceptance Criteria: 1. Given a desktop viewport at 1024px or wider, when the command center renders, then the mobile command panel and mobile action bar are hidden and the desktop frame/grid is visible. 2. Given a mobile viewport below 1024px, when the command center renders, then the desktop frame/grid is hidden and mobile tabs/actions are visible. 3. Browser screenshots show no duplicate command workflow at desktop width.
Expected Behavior: Desktop and mobile command layouts are mutually exclusive at their intended breakpoints.
Entry Points: Root command center at desktop and mobile responsive widths.
Edge Cases: Custom component CSS overriding Tailwind responsive utilities, tablet widths between 720px and 1024px, mobile action bar visibility, desktop wrapper display after production build.
User Roles / Permissions: Teacher / worksheet creator; no auth or permission gates in scope.
Error / Empty / Loading States: Duplicate layouts can appear after build when custom display rules override responsive utility classes.
Initial Test Evidence: failed: Visual inspection of output/playwright/real-browser-desktop.png showed the mobile command workflow rendered above the desktop workflow at 1440px width.
Reproduction Steps: 1. Build and start the static preview. 2. Open http://127.0.0.1:4173 at a 1440px Chromium viewport. 3. Capture a full-page screenshot. 4. Observe the mobile setup/tabs panel rendered above the desktop command layout.
Expected Result: Only the desktop command layout appears at wide viewport; mobile-only tabs/action bar/menu button are hidden.
Actual Result: Before fix, the mobile command panel was visible above the desktop layout at desktop width.
Root Cause: Custom .command-mobile display:grid CSS overrode the responsive lg:hidden utility, leaving mobile-only UI visible at desktop widths.
Screenshots / Evidence: output/playwright/real-browser-desktop.png before remediation showed duplicate mobile and desktop command workflows; final screenshot will be refreshed after retest. passed: Fresh Chromium QA verified desktop viewport shows only desktop command layout and mobile viewport shows only mobile command layout; see output/playwright/feature-story-real-browser-results.json.
Fix Summary: Added a command-desktop-frame class and explicit 1024px media rules to hide mobile-only UI at desktop widths and hide desktop frame/grid below desktop widths.
UX Improvement: Teachers now see a single viewport-appropriate workflow instead of duplicated controls.
Regression Evidence: passed: Fresh Chromium QA verified desktop viewport shows only desktop command layout and mobile viewport shows only mobile command layout; see output/playwright/feature-story-real-browser-results.json.
Notes: Discovered by inspecting saved Chromium screenshot during final audit completion checks.
